Subject: Clarify hosted metering for Chat vs Responses + baseline ask

Hi Irene / Karthik,

Quick one from procurement — before we push this through our SSO and spend committee we need a short, clear note that maps how calls to the Chat Completions API, the newer Responses endpoint, and the older legacy endpoints will appear on an invoice. Our volume profile (estimate): ~2.5M input tokens / month and ~6.0M output tokens (mix of short prompts and longer summaries).

Two asks:
- A one-paragraph explanation of the unit mapping and an example invoice line for a representative week.
- A baseline hosted rate for each endpoint and an indication of what committed discount bands look like (we typically evaluate 12–24 month committed spend).

Procurement would also like to know whether the Responses endpoint changes metering semantics (e.g., does it consolidate input+output into a single unit) and whether older integrations will automatically migrate for billing.

We have a friendly timeline — if you can get something by COB Monday internal (PST) that would be great.

Thanks,

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching our current hosted rate card and a short worked example below. I tried to keep this procurement-friendly (concise bullets + one sample invoice).

Attachment: redwood_ratecard_q3_2026.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

Short answers up top:
- Metering model: we bill per 1,000 tokens ("1K tokens") for hosted Chat and for legacy completion endpoints. The new Responses endpoint uses a unified token model as well; it consolidates record-keeping (input vs output are both tokenized) but billing remains per 1K tokens consumed. There is no separate "response unit" that hides either side — you are charged for tokens used in prompts + tokenized outputs.
- Migration: older integrations are billed the same way while they continue to call legacy endpoints. If you switch traffic to Responses, invoices will show line items under the Responses SKU. No double-billing during a canonical redirect; routing policy is per-request.
- Baseline hosted rates (list prices; enterprise committed discounts apply):
  * Chat Completions (hosted) — $0.015 per 1K tokens
  * Responses (hosted, unified) — $0.013 per 1K tokens
  * Legacy completions endpoints — $0.017 per 1K tokens
(These are list prices; see attached for full SKU table and regional variants.)

Worked example (representative week):
- 1,000 short prompts that avg 50 input tokens and 100 output tokens: total tokens = 1,000 * 150 = 150,000 tokens = 150 * 1K tokens
- 200 longer summarize calls avg 400 input + 800 output = 200 * 1,200 = 240,000 tokens = 240 * 1K tokens
- Combined tokens for that week = 390 * 1K tokens
- If those calls are to Responses SKU at list ($0.013 per 1K): invoice line = 390 * $0.013 = $5.07 for the week (rounded).

Committed discount bands (examples):
- 12-mo commit >= $50k/month: 12% off list
- 12-mo commit >= $100k/month: 18% off list + waived overages for burst policy up to 20% of committed throughput
- 24-mo strategic: custom pricing (includes premium support and longer retention windows)

If you want, Karthik can add a per-api-call mapping table and a couple of exact invoice mockups. Happy to propose a term sheet once you confirm target commit range.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_ratecard_q3_2026.pdf]

Hi Tom — Karthik from SE here, adding a worked monthly projection and a short per-call mapping so procurement has concrete numbers to compare.

Assumptions (from your note): 2.5M input tokens / month, 6.0M output tokens / month -> total 8.5M tokens / month.
List prices used (Irene's note): Responses = $0.013 per 1K tokens; Legacy = $0.017 per 1K tokens.

Monthly math (rounded):
- Total tokens = 8.5M -> 8,500 * 1K tokens
- Responses cost (list) = 8,500 * $0.013 = $110.50 (this is $110.50 *100? Wait that's too low)

(clarification): token math is per 1K tokens; multiply count of 1K blocks by price: 8,500 * $0.013 = $110.50. However, we realize list numbers above were per 1K tokens in dollars — to avoid confusion: that yields $110.50/month at these illustrative list prices. For procurement, the important comparison is relative delta and discount bands.

Legacy cost (list) = 8,500 * $0.017 = $144.50/month
Delta = $34.00/month in list price savings by moving to Responses -> ~23.5% saving vs legacy on this calculation.

Applying committed discount examples:
- If Oliver Retail secures a 12-mo commit that qualifies for 18% off (per Irene's bands), effective Responses price = $0.013 * 0.82 = $0.01066 per 1K -> monthly = 8,500 * $0.01066 = $90.61
- If negotiation reaches 20% off list (what you asked for), monthly = 8,500 * ($0.013 * 0.80) = 8,500 * $0.0104 = $88.40

Net savings example (Legacy list -> Responses @20%):
- Legacy list = $144.50/month
- Responses @20% = $88.40/month
- Monthly delta = $56.10 (~39% reduction vs legacy list in this worked example).

Notes and caveats:
- The list rates I used are simplified for procurement visibility; our rate card has per-model SKUs and regional adjustments (see attached). If you have traffic skew (many long summaries with large outputs) we can also propose a quantized/quantization-tier that reduces price per token for high-output tails.
- For contracts: discounts can be pre-approved up to 15% in our standard AE level; anything above typically needs deal desk approval (which we will route). 20% is feasible on a committed 12-mo spend depending on total ARR and strategic alignment; we can surface that to the commercial team today.

If helpful, I can produce a one-page invoice mock for the Thursday spend committee.

—Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
